subject.title: Feature Request: Gateway lifecycle hooks (onSubagentComplete, onToolCallThreshold, onTurnComplete)

question: Should OpenClaw expose subagent completion, turn completion, and tool-call threshold boundaries through HOOK.md workspace/internal hooks, typed plugin hooks only, or a split surface with different payload and authority levels?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent API affects trusted local code execution, session-state exposure, hook ordering, threshold configuration, and the boundary between workspace automation and plugin middleware.

options.title: Split Observation From Control
options.body: Expose minimal observation-oriented workspace events first, while keeping richer result, mutation, threshold, and policy behavior in typed plugin hooks.

options.title: Use Typed Plugin Hooks Only
options.body: Avoid new HOOK.md lifecycle events and extend the typed plugin API for lifecycle and receipt use cases that need stronger contracts.

options.title: Add Full Workspace Surface
options.body: Add subagent, turn-complete, and threshold workspace events after defining payload, ordering, redaction, and config semantics.

recommendation.title: Split Observation From Control
recommendation.body: Expose minimal observation-oriented workspace events first, while keeping richer result, mutation, threshold, and policy behavior in typed plugin hooks.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a product and security boundary choice across hook contracts rather than a line-level code repair.
